subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should subagent stall recovery be a subagent-specific default-on nudge-then-kill policy, an opt-in policy, or part of the broader session activity/watchdog design?
rationale: This choice changes runtime defaults, can kill in-flight work, and affects chat-channel delivery semantics, so code cannot safely pick the policy from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design subagent recovery first
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical subagent recovery item and specify activity source, thresholds, nudge delivery, kill semantics, and parent/channel notification before implementation.

options.title: Fold into session activity watchdog
options.body: Make the broader sessions.activity/watchdog issues canonical and treat this issue as a dependent subagent use case once that API exists.

options.title: Defer automatic recovery
options.body: Rely on explicit `runTimeoutSeconds` plus future manual kill/reap controls and do not add automatic stall intervention yet.

recommendation.title: Design subagent recovery first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical subagent recovery item and specify activity source, thresholds, nudge delivery, kill semantics, and parent/channel notification before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent timeout and steer/recovery history points to steipete as the best available owner for the product/runtime default decision.
